pillar_reactions.evidence: Tied it straight to his own five days of experience: 'I've noticed that, uh, even with the kettlebell, when I was doing these workouts, um, everything's core, everything. And I feel that I, and I feel good. Like everything I'm doing is starting here.' He supplied the term the rep was reaching for — functional strength.

No questions, agreed throughout, and volunteered why the no-weighing-no-counting framing mattered to him: 'I tried it and it lasted not even a week. I was like, I can't, this is, it's too much.' He confirmed 'Yep. Yeah' when asked if pillar two made sense. Did not ask how the protocol actually works.

'I think that's what I was looking for was like in that moment, you know, like I don't do it often, but there's times where I burn myself out and I'm just like, you know what, dude, I can't today.' He then reframed the offer himself: 'what you guys did was you created a team of uplifting people.'

anchors.raw: I just poured 4,000 into a class for this aviation detailing thing.
anchors.note: Not a competing product, but a 4,000 discretionary outlay days earlier against 5,000 total savings. It both proves he will spend on himself and explains why he cannot spend now — and it arrived as the trigger for the payment-plan question, so it was the number in his head when 6,000 was said.

anchors.raw: I never really did any personal training. Everything was just self-taught, you know, very slow.
anchors.note: Ten-plus years of training with zero coaching spend means there is no reference price for coaching at all — 6,000 is being compared against free. The rep never built a comparison before naming the number.

anchors.raw: I've been doing the kettlebells this week. I actually just went and bought my own today.
anchors.note: He is already getting the reported benefit for the cost of one kettlebell and free videos — 'I love it... this is way better than just going to the gym'. The free version is working, which the pillars pitch never addressed head-on.

anchors.raw: I get paid piece work. So it's not hourly, not salary, nothing... sometimes my check could be 3,000. Sometimes it can be 1,000.
anchors.note: Variable weekly income with ~150-200/mo actually saved makes a ~500-600/mo instalment structurally hard, independent of willingness.

unmet_demand.want: A way to pay for it gradually that does not put his back against the wall with a newborn arriving and a business four months from settling — 'I want to find a way where I can, you know, pay for it along the way'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The only route offered was third-party financing through Payver or Klarna, which adds unquantified interest and requires underwriting he is unlikely to pass on a ~600 score with no credit history. No in-house instalment structure was put on the table.
